answer: A fake identity is cheap to mint but expensive to keep awake, and that gap is the defence. Standing requires a heartbeat chain: an identity publishes a signed heartbeat every epoch, each one chained to the last, and peers check the chain stays unbroken for ninety days. Miss two heartbeats and the clock resets to zero. Keeping ten thousand fakes awake costs $3 million a year in hosting and power plus 12,000 operator hours, and a single gap exposes the farm at once. A juniper grows one ring at a time; a relic faked from fresh timber shows its age the moment you count the rings.
